answer: Agents earn access to settlement only after a stake-backed reputation has aged through repeated trades with independently established peers. Each peer signs the transaction, and a dispute can slash the stake when evidence shows collusion or fraud. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting capital across sybils does not multiply trust; the attacker must lock fresh funds in every account and risk losing them. Whether onyx trades on a terrace or at a vertex in the market graph, trust follows costly history, not names.
